title: What the Beloved does, I accept
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 187
summary: The shabad begins by yielding the argument with what the Beloved does. It moves into single-hearted reliance until even honor itself is handed back to the One who gave it.
whyItMatters: This is for the person exhausting themselves by resisting the day, the loss, or the unanswered turn. Held steadily, it changes complaint into trust and loosens the fear that acceptance means abandonment.
takeaway: Let the Beloved's way grow dearer than the mind's protest.

lines.translation: Whatever my Friend does, I accept.
My Friend's actions are pleasing to me. ||1||
Within my conscious mind, the One Lord is my only Support.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸੁ ਕਿਛੁ ਕਰਣਾ ਸੁ ਹਮਰਾ ਮੀਤ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: jis kichh karanaa su hamaraa meet ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: One who does this is my Friend. ||1||Pause||
By Guru's Grace, I give my love to Him. ||2||
My Friend is the Inner-knower, the Searcher of hearts.
He is the All-powerful Being, the Supreme Lord and Master. ||3||
I am Your servant; You are my Lord and Master.
Nanak: my honor and glory are Yours, God. ||4||40||109||

structure: It opens with bare consent: what the Beloved does is received, not argued with.
The middle gathers the heart around one support, naming the Lord as the inner-knower and only true stay.
It ends in belonging: servant and Master, honor and glory returned to God alone.
